title: Read out the one page checkout experiment
businessContext: The checkout_one_page experiment has finished and product wants a go or no go. Arjun asks for the standard readout: per variant, how many visitors were assigned, how many of them purchased while the experiment was running and the relative lift of treatment over control. Conversion is measured per visitor, from the moment of assignment until the experiment ended.
requirements: Take the experiment with experiment_key 'checkout_one_page' from web.experiments and its assignments from web.experiment_assignments.
A visitor converts when web.events has a 'purchase' event for the same visitor_id with event_at at or after assigned_at and before the experiment ended_at.
Return per variant the assigned visitors, converting visitors and the conversion rate in percent rounded to 2 decimals.
lift_vs_control_pct is the relative difference between the variant rate and the control rate in percent, computed from unrounded rates and rounded to 2 decimals; it is null for the control row.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly two rows, control and treatment.
Columns are variant, visitors, converting_visitors, conversion_rate_pct and lift_vs_control_pct, in that order.
Purchases made before assignment or after the experiment ended do not count.
referenceSql:
WITH experiment AS (
  SELECT experiment_id, COALESCE(ended_at, TIMESTAMPTZ 'infinity') AS ended_at
  FROM web.experiments
  WHERE experiment_key = 'checkout_one_page'
),
visitor_outcomes AS (
  SELECT a.variant,
         a.visitor_id,
         EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM web.events AS e
           WHERE e.visitor_id = a.visitor_id
             AND e.event_name = 'purchase'
             AND e.event_at >= a.assigned_at
             AND e.event_at < x.ended_at
         ) AS converted
  FROM web.experiment_assignments AS a
  JOIN experiment AS x ON x.experiment_id = a.experiment_id
),
variant_rates AS (
  SELECT variant,
         COUNT(*) AS visitors,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE converted) AS converting_visitors,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE converted)::numeric / COUNT(*) AS conversion_rate
  FROM visitor_outcomes
  GROUP BY variant
)
SELECT v.variant,
       v.visitors,
       v.converting_visitors,
       ROUND(100 * v.conversion_rate, 2) AS conversion_rate_pct,
       CASE
         WHEN v.variant = 'control' THEN NULL
         ELSE ROUND(100 * (v.conversion_rate - c.conversion_rate) / NULLIF(c.conversion_rate, 0), 2)
       END AS lift_vs_control_pct
FROM variant_rates AS v
CROSS JOIN (SELECT conversion_rate FROM variant_rates WHERE variant = 'control') AS c
ORDER BY v.variant;
hints: Build one row per assigned visitor with a converted flag; EXISTS against web.events with the time bounds works well.
Aggregate per variant and keep the unrounded rate in a CTE so you can reuse it for the lift.
CROSS JOIN the control row to every variant and compute (rate - control_rate) / control_rate * 100.
explanation: Conversion is defined per visitor, so the analysis starts at assignment grain and checks for a purchase in the exposure window with EXISTS. Keeping the raw rates in a CTE avoids compounding rounding errors when the lift is computed, and cross joining the single control row makes the comparison explicit.
